traditional_principles_embodied: Independent vowels precede consonants (a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ, e, ai, o, au)
Consonants follow classical Paninian vargas (ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, antastha, ushman)
Within a base consonant, full syllabic vocalizations (ka, kā, ki, kī, ku, kū, kṛ, kṝ, ke, kai, ko, kau) precede pure consonant conjuncts (k + virama + C)
Anusvara and Visarga are treated as secondary syllable-closing modifiers
Vedic accents (udatta, anudatta, svarita) act as quaternary tie-breakers
IAST romanization accurately preserves Sanskrit varnamala order rather than Latin alphabet order (e.g. ā precedes b, ṛ precedes e)
documentation.explicit_lexicographical_scope_and_bound: While this collator implements the syllabic ordering principles recognized by V.S. Apte (The Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary, 1890) and Sir M. Monier-Williams (Sanskrit-English Dictionary, 1899), it is formally classified as an 'Implementation-Specific Scholarly Profile'. It does not claim 100% facsimile equivalence to historical print dictionaries for complex prefix-compound decomposition or editorial headword lemmatization.
